blocks.raw: <Tip>The slope of the elastic region IS the Modulus of Elasticity. The slope of the unloading line (even from deep in the plastic region) also equals E. This parallelism is your memory anchor: elastic behavior is reversible, even if permanent strain remains.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing proportional limit with elastic limit. The proportional limit marks where Hooke's Law stops holding mathematically. The elastic limit marks where the material stops returning to zero strain. These are close but distinct.","Assuming the yield point and elastic limit are the same thing. They are not. The elastic limit comes first; permanent deformation begins there. The yield point (in materials with a yield plateau) comes after, marked by a horizontal or near-flat region.","Misreading the stress axis. Stress is force divided by original (not current) area. This is engineering stress, not true stress. Confusion here leads to wrong numerical answers.","Treating E as variable across steel grades. E = 200,000 MPa for all structural steel grades. Only Fy and Fu change. Grade 50 and A36 have the same E.","Thinking rupture and ultimate strength are the same. Ultimate strength (UTS) is the peak of the curve. Rupture is where the material breaks completely. The difference between them represents necking and final fracture."] />
